scars.description: Diagnosed a 'Digital Crash' as physical failure. Assemblers were using excessive force to seat components, flexing the PCB and 'crushing' the traces (Mechanical Violence). Remedied by relieving interference points.
scars.label: The Thumb of God

scars.description: Managed a logistics empire of 400 unique SKUs. Salvaged a 50-unit pilot build and a 300-unit production run that were destined for the scrap heap.
scars.label: The Logistics Empire

scars.description: The IR lens was too tall (0.60 vs 0.36 clearance). Instead of cutting a new mold ($/Time), I modified the doorframe tool to remove interference, preserving the schedule and budget.
scars.label: 0-to-1 Tooling Save

scars.description: Dialed fans to the 7-8V sweet spot, reducing acoustic intensity by 30%. Turned an industrial machine into a whisper-quiet office device.
scars.label: Acoustic Silence

quotes: Jenim could not talk to Chip. That's the error. Right on the screen. A total crash loop.
It wasn't the silicon at all. Eric Norris pins it on the thumb of God.
If you don't respect the actual physics of assembly, the thumb of God is going to find your project and is going to crush it.
